#
# This exists because the removal was silently reverted twice by an external
# sync writing over `expo/package.json` and `expo/metro.config.js`. A revert is
# invisible in normal development — the vendor package is not installed here, so
# nothing breaks until a build runs on a machine that does have it. This job runs
# on every push and PR, so a revert fails loudly instead of silently restoring
# the dependency.
#
# GitHub is the source of truth. If this job is green on `main`, the app on
# `main` builds without the vendor. That is what independence means in practice.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  independence:
    name: Zero-vendor runtime + build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.9

      - name: Vendor package must be absent from the app manifest
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          echo "::group::expo/package.json"
          node -e '
            const pkg = require("./expo/package.json");
            const hits = [];
            for (const section of ["dependencies", "devDependencies", "peerDependencies", "optionalDependencies"]) {
              for (const name of Object.keys(pkg[section] || {})) {
                if (name.toLowerCase().includes("rork")) hits.push(section + ":" + name);
              }
            }
            if (hits.length) {
              console.error("FAIL - vendor package present: " + hits.join(", "));
              process.exit(1);
            }
            console.log("PASS - no vendor package in any dependency section");
          '
          echo "::endgroup::"

      - name: Metro config must be a self-contained Expo config
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if grep -qi "rork" expo/metro.config.js; then
            echo "FAIL - expo/metro.config.js references the vendor toolkit."
            echo "This makes the vendor a HARD build dependency: no APK, AAB or"
            echo "web bundle can be produced on a machine without it."
            grep -ni "rork" expo/metro.config.js
            exit 1
          fi
          grep -q "expo/metro-config" expo/metro.config.js
          echo "PASS - metro.config.js is stock Expo"

      - name: Babel transformer must not delegate to the vendor
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if grep -qi "rork-ai" expo/scripts/ivx-metro-transformer.js; then
            echo "FAIL - the bundler hot path can still load vendor code."
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "PASS - transformer delegates to Expo only"

      - name: App runtime must not call vendor servers
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          RUNTIME_DIRS="expo/app expo/components expo/lib expo/hooks expo/constants"

          fi

            echo "FAIL - app runtime reads a vendor environment variable"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "PASS - zero vendor URLs, zero vendor env vars in app runtime"

      - name: Install with the vendor registry scope blocked
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd expo
          # Proves the install needs nothing from the vendor scope. If any
          # manifest still asked for it, resolution fails here.
          bun install --frozen-lockfile

          fi
          echo "PASS - install is clean and vendor-free"

      - name: Zero-vendor runtime audit
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd expo
          node scripts/verify-zero-rork-runtime.mjs

      - name: Metro must resolve and bundle without the vendor
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd expo
          # Loading the config is the real proof: the old config called
          # require("@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk/metro") at module scope and threw here.
          node -e '
            const config = require("./metro.config.js");
            if (!config || !config.transformer) throw new Error("metro config did not load");
            console.log("PASS - metro config loaded with no vendor package installed");
            console.log("transformer:", require("path").basename(config.transformer.babelTransformerPath));
          '

      - name: Independence regression tests
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cd expo
          bun test __tests__/metro-ai-sdk-compatibility.test.ts __tests__/tabs-auth-error-latch.test.ts

      - name: Summary
        if: success()
        shell: bash
        run: |
          {
            echo "## IVX Independence Gate — PASS"
            echo ""
            echo "Verified on GitHub runners, with no vendor package installed:"
            echo ""
            echo "- vendor absent from every dependency section of \`expo/package.json\`"
            echo "- \`expo/metro.config.js\` is a self-contained Expo config"
            echo "- the babel transformer delegates to Expo only"
            echo "- app runtime has zero vendor URLs and zero vendor env vars"
            echo "- \`bun install --frozen-lockfile\` resolves clean, \`node_modules/@rork-ai\` absent"
            echo "- Metro config loads and resolves without the vendor package"
            echo ""
            echo "Commit: \`$GITHUB_SHA\`"
          } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

## The lock-in was real — not branding

`expo/metro.config.js` was six lines; line 2 required the vendor at module scope and exported `withRorkMetro(config)`. **No APK, AAB or web bundle could be built on any machine without that package.**

And it was **silently reverted twice** by a platform sync during our session — I caught it live:

```
metro.config.js -> back to require("@rork-ai/toolkit-sdk/metro")
package.json    -> @rork-ai/toolkit-sdk reinjected
node_modules    -> package NOT on disk
```

A revert is invisible locally (nothing's installed, nothing breaks) — it only breaks on the machine that ships your product. That's why enforcement moved to GitHub.

## Evidence — verified on `main`, not the sandbox

```

expo/metro.config.js  vendor refs: 0  -> stock Expo config
BUILD SUCCESSFUL 1m 19s  with node_modules/@rork-ai ABSENT
```

```
  ascii=none   utf16=none
```

App runtime: **0 vendor URLs, 0 vendor env vars.**

I also removed a subtle one: the babel transformer used to try the vendor first and fall back to Expo — so vendor code stayed on the bundler hot path whenever installed, meaning **two machines could bundle identical source differently.** Expo-only now.

## Enforcement so it can't come back
